company_items.summary: AutoZone posted fiscal Q4 EPS of $56.05 versus the Street's $54.03, but the beat was low quality — 145 basis points of gross margin tailwind from tariff refunds and 105 basis points from a non-cash LIFO benefit inflated results. Domestic comps came in at plus 1.6% versus the expected plus 3.1%, and the operating expense ratio rose 100 basis points year-over-year to 33.4% of sales. Management noted improving sales linearity in the final eight weeks and expressed confidence in fiscal 2027 growth.

Cognex announced the acquisition of RealSense, the market leader in depth-sensing cameras and vision technology for robotic perception and Physical AI, for approximately $500 million upfront plus an additional $106.5 million. RealSense is expected to generate $80 to $90 million in revenue, representing more than 50% year-over-year growth. The deal positions Cognex at the intersection of machine vision and the fast-growing Physical AI theme.

MillerKnoll reported fiscal Q1 EPS of 53 cents versus the Street's 36 cents, and notably the beat holds up even excluding an 11-cent tariff refund tailwind, with adjusted EPS of 42 cents still beating consensus. Sales missed, declining 3.3% organically to $923.4 million versus the expected $943.2 million, though orders grew 3.5% year-over-year. Fiscal 2027 revenue guidance was trimmed to $3.88 to $4.03 billion from $3.93 to $4.13 billion, while EPS guidance of $1.85 to $2.15 was held unchanged.

Pentair named Bob Hau as its new CFO, effective November 1, with current interim CFO Bob Fishman staying on through that date to ensure a smooth transition. Hau brings prior CFO experience at Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox International. The leadership change is a routine corporate development with no financial guidance update attached.

THOR Industries missed fiscal Q4 EPS at 78 cents versus the Street's 87 cents, with gross margins falling 230 basis points year-over-year to 12.4% versus the expected 13.85%. Management cited stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, and inflation straining household budgets and keeping retail soft, and expects a relatively flat retail environment in fiscal 2027. Some bright spots include healthy dealer inventory levels, structural cost reduction actions underway, and a roughly 75% surge in the North America towable RV order backlog year-over-year.

Viking Therapeutics shares spiked in pre-market trading after the company reported positive clinical trial results for its GLP-1 drug VK2735, showing 22% weight loss. The result is a significant readout for Viking's obesity pipeline and reinforces competitive positioning in the GLP-1 space against larger rivals. This is a high-profile catalyst likely to move the broader weight-loss drug sector in early trading.

sectors: The GLP-1 and obesity drug space is in focus following Viking Therapeutics' positive VK2735 trial data showing 22% weight loss, which could lift sector peers. The RV and outdoor recreation space faces headwinds per THOR Industries' cautious commentary on interest rates, fuel costs, and soft retail demand. The Physical AI and robotics theme gets a data point from Cognex's RealSense acquisition.
tts_summary:
Good morning. This is the Tuesday September 22nd company-specific earnings brief. There's no broad macro or index commentary in today's note — this is a pure stock catalyst edition, so let's get right into it.

Starting with the biggest mover: Viking Therapeutics is spiking in pre-market after reporting positive trial results for its GLP-1 drug VK2735, showing 22% weight loss. That is a meaningful number and a genuine catalyst — expect the broader obesity and weight-loss drug space to trade up in sympathy at the open.

On AutoZone — the headline fiscal fourth quarter EPS beat looks good at $56.05 versus the Street's $54.03, but peel it back and it's low quality. About 145 basis points of gross margin benefit came from tariff refunds, and another 105 basis points from a non-cash LIFO adjustment. Strip those out and the underlying business looks softer — domestic comps came in at plus 1.6% against an expectation of plus 3.1%, and the operating expense ratio worsened by 100 basis points year-over-year. Management did flag improving sales linearity in the back half of the quarter and said they feel well positioned for fiscal 2027 growth, but the market may look through the headline beat here.

Cognex is acquiring RealSense — the market leader in depth-sensing cameras and vision technology for robotic perception and Physical AI — for roughly $500 million upfront plus another $106 million. RealSense is expected to do $80 to $90 million in revenue, growing more than 50% year-over-year. This is a clean strategic fit and plugs Cognex directly into the Physical AI infrastructure buildout theme.

MillerKnoll beat cleanly on fiscal first quarter earnings — 53 cents versus the Street's 36 cents — and importantly, the beat holds up even after stripping out an 11-cent tariff refund tailwind. Adjusted that's still 42 cents against a 36-cent consensus. Sales missed, down 3.3% organically, but orders grew 3.5% year-over-year. Guidance is a slight trim on the top line but EPS is unchanged. Net-net, a solid print.

THOR Industries is the weak link this morning. Fiscal fourth quarter EPS came in at 78 cents versus 87 cents expected, with gross margins falling 230 basis points year-over-year to 12.4%. Management's tone was cautious — calling out stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, and inflation pressuring household budgets throughout the critical selling season. They're not providing formal fiscal 2027 guidance until later in the fall and expect a relatively flat retail environment. The one silver lining is the North America towable RV order backlog surged roughly 75% year-over-year.

Finally, Pentair named Bob Hau as its new CFO effective November 1st. He brings prior CFO experience at Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox International. Routine transition, no financial update attached.

Bottom line for today: Viking is the headline mover and could lift GLP-1 peers. AutoZone's beat is hollow. THOR is a cautious read on the rate-sensitive consumer. And Cognex is making a smart bet on Physical AI. Watch how the broader tape absorbs these prints — it's a stock-picker's session more than a macro-driven one.
